title: Forces, density and pressure

parts.text:
15 The diagrams show three rigid objects P, Q and R being subjected to different combinations of
forces.
P
Q
R
30
30
80 N
50 N
50 N

10 N

Which objects are in equilibrium?
A
P and Q
B
P and R
C
Q and R
D
none of them

hints: Notice for P that the leftward $10\text{ N} + 20\text{ N}$ balances the rightward $20\text{ N} + 10\text{ N}$, so check moments separately by combining the top pair and bottom pair.
For Q compare the $80\text{ N}$ upward pair with the $60\text{ N}$ downward pair along the symmetric diagonals, and for R resolve the two $50\text{ N}$ forces at $30^{\circ}$ to the vertical.
Recall rigid-body equilibrium needs both zero vector sum of forces and zero resultant moment, so test both conditions for each of P, Q and R.
walkthrough: For a rigid object, equilibrium requires resultant force $= 0$ in any direction and resultant moment $= 0$ about any point.

Object P: resultant horizontal force $= (20+10) - (10+20) = 0\text{ N}$. However the top gives $20-10 = 10\text{ N}$ to the right and the bottom gives $20-10 = 10\text{ N}$ to the left, forming a clockwise couple with non-zero moment. So P is not in equilibrium.

Object Q: left-right symmetry cancels horizontal components, but vertically the two $80\text{ N}$ forces act upward and the two $60\text{ N}$ forces act downward along the same diagonal lines. The upward vertical component exceeds the downward vertical component, so resultant force is upward and non-zero. So Q is not in equilibrium.

Object R: horizontal components $50\sin30^{\circ}$ to left and right cancel. Vertical upward force $= 2 \times 50\cos30^{\circ} = 100 \times 0.866 = 86.6\text{ N}$, while downward force $= 100\text{ N}$. Net force $= 100 - 86.6 = 13.4\text{ N}$ downward, so R is not in equilibrium.
Since P, Q and R each fail at least one equilibrium condition, none of them is in equilibrium. This is option D.

A.explanation: P has zero resultant force but a non-zero resultant moment, and Q has a non-zero resultant force, so neither is in equilibrium.

B.explanation: P has a clockwise couple from the $10\text{ N}$ net forces top and bottom, and R has a net downward force, so neither is in equilibrium.

C.explanation: Q has larger $80\text{ N}$ upward forces than $60\text{ N}$ downward forces, and R has upward components less than $100\text{ N}$, so neither has zero resultant force.

D.explanation: P fails the zero moment condition, while Q and R fail the zero resultant force condition, so none is in equilibrium.
